title: decode_limited() O(max_bytes) claim is wrong — splits all input into lines first
description: The doc comment says 'This makes preview queries O(max_bytes) rather than O(input)' but this is inaccurate. The function begins with: let lines: Vec<&[u8]> = input.split(...).collect() — this walks all of input and builds a Vec of all lines, O(input) time and O(number-of-lines) space. The begin_idx search is also O(input). Only the *decoding* of data lines is O(max_bytes). For large UU-encoded attachments (hundreds of KB), a max_bytes=100 preview call still pays the full input-splitting cost. A line-by-line iterator approach (without collect()) would achieve true O(max_bytes) after the begin line is found. The allocation for decoded data is bounded (correct), but the claim in the doc is misleading. At scale: a 1 MB UU attachment previewed at 100 bytes does O(1 MB) work instead of O(100 bytes).
close_reason: Replaced false O(max_bytes) claim with accurate complexity note explaining O(input) line-split up-front.
